content: We don't know if infusing items with mana influences the world around us.
This is because the current generation of Elemancers are new to these lands and haven't gotten enough knowledge to look at these aspects of the world just yet.
Maybe with the passing of time, Elemancers will grow stronger and more knowledgeable.
Perhaps then they might invent new devices and machinations that will help them monitor the world around them better.
Muscles reduce the natural flow of mana in untrained Elemancers.
Because of this, it's advised for people who wish to dabble in Elemancy to use their offhand for mana manipulation.

This one is usually less used than your dominant hand, which is used for swinging swords and tools, and has less muscles in them because of this, making mana flow just that little bit easier through your offhand.
Most Elemancers keep this habit even later through their lives and stick with using their offhand for mana manipulation.
From the interaction with infused materials, we can conclude that the colour of mana is cyan.
Elemancers noticed this from looking at materials like Infused Wool or Infused Ingots.
The infusion drains the wool of colour and a cyan sheen can be observed afterwards.
While infusing copper adds the cyan to the red-brownish colour of the metal resulting in the pink-purple ingot.
As to why mana is cyan, we can only guess. The main theory is that mana is the inverse of lifeblood, likewise, the inverse of the colour red is cyan.
